summary: A hostile dwarf's wand of undead turning hits the hero, who carries a lichen corpse. C revives the corpse before the next turn boundary; JavaScript skips zap.c:unturn_you from muse.c:mbhitm, so revival and the resulting monster placement never occur.

source.branch: In mbhitm's WAN_UNDEAD_TURNING arm, a hit on the hero calls unturn_you(). A hit on another monster calls unturn_dead(mtmp); its nonzero result sets wake before undead resistance and wakeup handling.
callers: The selected recording reaches mhitu.c:mattacku() -> muse.c:use_offensive() -> mbhit() -> mbhitm() for a monster's wand of undead turning. The JavaScript route is unported_monster_actions.js:useOffensiveItem() -> muse.js:use_offensive() -> mbhit() -> mbhitm().

The active defensive route is monmove.c:dochug()/monmove() -> muse.c:use_defensive() -> mbhit() -> mbhitm(); the JavaScript routes are monmove.js:use_defensive() and unported_monster_actions.js:usePreMoveItems() -> muse.js:use_defensive().
dependencies: zap.c:unturn_you() already has a JavaScript implementation in js/zap.js, but it is private and muse.js currently records note_unported('zap.c unturn_you'). Exporting and calling it will reuse that implementation.
zap.c:unturn_dead() already returns the revived-corpse count in js/zap.js. muse.js currently records note_unported('zap.c unturn_dead') instead of using that result to gate wakeup.

zap.c:revive() and its makemon_revival() call shape already exist in the accepted-base JavaScript implementation. A2 currently owns source:makemon.c:makemon; the replay must not prompt edits to that scope without fresh evidence of a separate placement defect.
